Subject: Proposed Order Form redlines: SLA & maintenance (ACME)

Karen — attaching our draft redlines to the Order Form & SLA. High-level calls: we need to tighten up the uptime target language and cap aggregate service credits to manage financial exposure. Key asks from our side: 

- Uptime: leave base at 99.9% but carve a sequence-length / scheduled-maintenance exclusion that’s explicit.
- Service credits: capped at 20% of monthly recurring fees per billing period (see attached).
- Response times: P1 (Production down) — initial response within 1 hour, mitigation plan within 4 hours; P2 — 4 hours initial response.
- Maintenance windows: propose a 2-hour maintenance window per week or a monthly 4-hour scheduled window with minimum 72-hour notice; emergency maintenance only with post-notice within 24 hours.

I'm looping in Laura and Marissa to confirm commercial tradeoffs. Please review and let us know Acme legal's priority points so we can take a clean position to legal. Attachment: ACME_Redlines_20270220.docx (redline).

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the redlines. Quick reaction from Acme legal/procurement: we can accept a capped credit structure but cannot accept a cap below 50% for systemic outages; uptime target should be 99.95% for the core inference endpoint (we run customer-facing flows). Maintenance notice needs to be 7 days for planned work; emergency maintenance must be limited and compensated if it causes downtime.

I attached our counter-redline. Main points:
- Uptime: 99.95% for endpoint ‘/v1/generate’ only; fallbacks allowed for non-core models.
- Credits: uncapped for severity-1 events (we propose uncapped until investigation complete) and 50% cap per month otherwise.
- Response SLOs: P1 initial response within 30 minutes; P2 within 2 hours.
- Maintenance: 7 days notice for scheduled; any monthly maintenance to be limited to 2 hours.

We need to escalate commercial options if we can't align on availability terms — this is a deal-driver for Acme. See attached: ACME_Counter_Redlines_20270220.docx.

—Karen

Team — forwarding Acme's reply (excerpted above). They're pushing hard on uptime (99.95%) and much tighter response SLOs. My read: Acme will make availability and credits a gating item for signature. Proposed internal posture: 

1) Make a commercial exception for this strategic logo: offer 99.95% but only for the primary HTTP endpoint and only for requests that meet a defined request profile (payload size, model family). This lets us avoid tail cases.
2) Keep a capped-credit model but increase to 30% (compromise) with an uncapped investigation credit for verified systemic incidents only (time-boxed).
3) Response SLOs — we can shorten to P1 1 hour (initial) / mitigation 4 hours; pushing to 30min increases ops risk. Suggest we offer 1 hour with a whitepaper on incident handling and optional 24/7 dedicated support at additional cost.
4) Maintenance — accept 7-day notice for standard maintenance; require a maximum 4 hours per month and 72-hour notice for non-critical ops.

Next actions: 
- Dev, can you draft precise language for the maintenance and credits carveouts (I copied you)?
- Laura, confirm whether commercial can accept 30% cap and where that hits the quote.
- Marissa, prep a short note explaining how our incident response mapping works for the legal team (we can attach to the counter).

I want to be ready for a call with Acme legal early next week.

Jonas

Jonas / team — drafting proposed contract language below (high-level snippets you can paste into the Order Form / SLA redline):

1) Availability definition (suggested):
"Availability" means the percentage of successful HTTP responses to valid requests to the primary inference endpoint '/v1/generate' measured over each billing month, excluding authorized maintenance and factors outside Supplier's reasonable control. The measurement excludes requests that exceed documented payload size or require non-standard model families (see Appendix A request profile).

2) Service Credits (suggested):
- If Availability < 99.95% for the primary endpoint in a billing month, Customer may request Service Credits up to 30% of the monthly recurring fees for that month.
- For verified systemic incidents caused by Supplier negligence resulting in material customer impact, Supplier will provide an additional investigatory credit determined after root-cause analysis, not to exceed a single additional month's MRR (one-time).

3) Response Times (suggested):
- Priority 1 (production down): initial acknowledgement within 1 hour; mitigation plan within 4 hours.
- Priority 2 (degraded performance): initial acknowledgement within 4 hours.

4) Scheduled Maintenance
- Supplier shall provide at least seventy-two (72) hours' prior notice for scheduled maintenance except where 7 days' notice is requested by Customer for non-emergency changes. Planned maintenance shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month for the primary endpoint.

Rationale: these terms strike a balance between Acme's uptime needs and our operational constraints. If they insist on 30-minute acknowledgements or uncapped credits for all outages, we need a priced support add-on (24/7 elite support) or a bespoke SLA amendment.

I'll drop these snippets into the redline and upload to the shared Drive.
